name: Vigilance for AI Medical Devices
blurb: Monitoring AI devices once they are in use.
title: Vigilance for AI Medical Devices
answer: Device vigilance adds a second layer for AI products: makers must collect and act on real world performance data after launch. WHO guidance on post-market surveillance and studies showing recalls in around 6 percent of FDA cleared AI devices underline why.

reading.body:
Post-market surveillance is the part of AI medical device regulation that starts after approval, and roughly 6.3 percent of FDA cleared AI devices had been recalled.

The WHO published guidance on post-market surveillance of medical devices in 2020, which sets the expectation that makers collect and act on real world performance data once a device is in use. The recall figure shows that expectation is not hypothetical. A cleared device can still fail in the field, and the failure is only visible through monitoring after launch.

For AI products this matters because the model is not fixed at approval. Performance drifts as clinical practice, patient mix, and data sources change, so the complaint and performance data a manufacturer collects has to feed back into model monitoring, not only into the complaint system. That is the operational difference between device vigilance and ordinary pharmacovigilance.

The data covers two points, a 2020 WHO guidance and a 2025 recall study, and does not say which devices were recalled, why, or how the 6.3 percent compares with non-AI devices. It also does not describe any specific monitoring method or regulatory requirement beyond the existence of the guidance.
